title: Basic Usage of NLMR
text: NLMR exposes 15 exported landscape-generation functions covering 16 algorithm variants. variants span spectrum spatial structure, spatially random landscapes (nlm_random) intermediate patterned forms deterministic planar gradients (nlm_planargradient) (see Palmer 1992). curdling generator, nlm_curds(), can produce either random curdling wheyed curdling, package one algorithm variant exported function. full browseable catalog generators, use catalog_nlm(). plot shows basic random landscape intentional spatial structure. simple random landscape can generated like :
code: x <- NLMR::nlm_random(ncol = 100, nrow = 100) terra::plot(x)

title: Basic Usage of NLMR
text: NLM rasters can combined create new landscape patterns. base raster can added one secondary rasters, optional scaling factors controlling strongly secondary raster contributes. example combines gradient random variation create complex surface.
code: base <- NLMR::nlm_edgegradient(ncol = 100, nrow = 100) secondary_1 <- NLMR::nlm_distancegradient(   ncol = 100,   nrow = 100,   origin = c(10, 10, 10, 10) ) secondary_2 <- NLMR::nlm_random(ncol = 100, nrow = 100)  combined <- base + (secondary_1 + secondary_2 * 0.2) terra::plot(combined)

title: Basic Usage of NLMR
text: Landscape rasters generated NLMR continuous default often fall 0 1. Use landscape_classify() convert continuous raster categorical classes want discrete landscape representation. example turns continuous gradient four discrete classes.
code: continuous <- NLMR::nlm_edgegradient(ncol = 100, nrow = 100) classified <- landscape_classify(continuous, n = 4) terra::plot(classified)

title: Simulating Neutral Landscape Models
text: NLMR R package simulating neutral landscape models (NLM). Designed generic framework like NLMpy, leverages ability simulate common NLM described ecological literature. NLMR builds advantages terra package returns simulations SpatRaster objects, thus ensuring direct compatibility common GIS tasks flexible simple usage. Furthermore, simulates NLMs within self-contained, reproducible framework.

title: landscape_classify — landscape_classify
text: Mode 1: Calculate optimum breakpoints using Jenks natural     breaks optimization, number classes determined `n`.     Jenks optimization seeks minimize variance within categories,     maximizing variance categories. Mode 2: number elements weighting vector determines number classes     resulting matrix. classes start value 1.     non-numerical levels required, user can specify vector turn     numerical factors data types, example character strings (.e. class labels).     numerical vector weightings sum 1, sum     weightings divided number elements weightings vector used classification. Mode 3: given 'real' landscape number classes weightings     extracted used classify given landscape (given weighting parameter     overwritten case!). optional mask value given corresponding     class 'real' landscape cut landscape beforehand. Missing values preserved. Tied values remain class, result can contain fewer classes requested.

title: nlm_mpd — nlm_mpd
text: algorithm direct implementation midpoint displacement algorithm. performs following steps: Initialization: Determine smallest fit  max(ncol, nrow) n^2 + 1 assign value n.  Setup matrix size (n^2 + 1)*(n^2 + 1).  Afterwards, assign random value four corners matrix. Square Step: square matrix, assign average  four corner points plus random value midpoint square. Diamond Step: diamond matrix, assign average  four corner points plus random value midpoint  diamond. iteration roughness, approximation common Hurst exponent, reduced.
